title: Man’s Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
target_audience: Readers seeking inspiration during times of suffering or adversity
Students and professionals in psychology, psychotherapy, or counseling
Individuals interested in Holocaust testimony and human resilience
Anyone searching for personal meaning or purpose in life
core_themes: The importance of purpose and hope
Personal responsibility in shaping one’s life
The psychology of survival and mental strength
primary_purpose: To share Viktor Frankl’s experiences as a Holocaust survivor and psychiatrist, illustrating how the search for meaning is the fundamental driving force in human life and offering lessons on resilience amid the harshest circumstances.

structure_format.organization: Divided into two main parts: Frankl’s concentration camp memoir, and an introduction to logotherapy (Frankl's theoretical framework)
features: Vivid, firsthand accounts of concentration camp life

key_concepts_lessons: Even under extreme suffering, individuals retain the freedom to choose their response and find meaning.
Meaning can be discovered through work, relationships, and how we approach unavoidable suffering.
Purpose and hope are fundamental to psychological health and survival.
Logotherapy centers on the ‘will to meaning’ rather than the Freudian ‘will to pleasure’ or Adlerian ‘will to power’.
Personal responsibility is key: each person must answer for their own life and choices.
Resilience is fostered by focusing on the future and on what one still has to live for.
notable_features: Firsthand Holocaust testimony paired with logotherapy insights
Broad applicability: cited in psychology, counseling, education, and personal development
Often quoted and referenced across disciplines
cultural_historical_context: Written shortly after World War II, Frankl’s book was among the first psychological reflections on surviving the Holocaust. It provided both a personal testimony and a universal message of hope and meaning in the face of suffering, greatly influencing existential psychology and popular understandings of resilience.
reception_impact: Recognized as one of the most influential books of the 20th century
Sold over 16 million copies and translated into dozens of languages
Praised for blending profound philosophical questions with practical psychological guidance
Endorsed by figures in psychology, medicine, religion, and education
Inspired generations coping with adversity and existential crises

When Breath Becomes Air by Paul Kalanithi
